nodes.label: HK Financial Job-Market Intelligence Platform
nodes.rationale: A daily-run Python backend that scrapes HK financial employers, enriches with AI, stores in one SQLite file, and feeds four delivery surfaces. Documented as 176 files, 7 scrape sources, 190+ companies, 5,000+ active jobs, read from the repo on 2026-07-23.

nodes.label: Adapter Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Nothing downstream of an adapter ever knows which website a job came from. That single rule is what keeps 190+ companies and 7 wildly different sources manageable; every adapter implements fetch_jobs() -> list[Job] against BaseAdapter.

nodes.label: Canonical Job Model
nodes.rationale: Defined once in hk_jobs/schema.py; called the single most important abstraction in the repo. Adapters translate into it, everything downstream only reads from it. Carries source/source_id dedup key, board_signals, source_tier, cross_posted, and dedup_hash() = sha256(company_slug + title + first_location)[:12] to catch the same vacancy on 2+ boards.

nodes.label: Adapter Priority Fallback Chain
nodes.rationale: Sources are tried in priority order per company: Workday, Eightfold, eFinancialCareers, JobsDB, Indeed, LinkedIn guest, longtail LLM. For Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and DBS, Indeed is promoted from fallback to primary because their clean JobsDB presence is near-zero.

nodes.label: Graceful Per-Company Failure (_safe_fetch)
nodes.rationale: Every adapter is wrapped in _safe_fetch() so an exception logs and returns [] instead of killing the run. One broken adapter never stops the other 189.

nodes.label: Longtail LLM Adapter
nodes.rationale: For boutique firms with no structured feed: LLM extraction straight from the company's own careers HTML, configured separately in companies_longtail.yaml. The only adapter emitting extraction_confidence, and the origin of the 'boutique' source_tier.

nodes.label: Six-Phase Daily Pipeline

nodes.label: Daily Automation via daily_run.sh Cron

nodes.label: DeepSeek AI Enrichment Pass

Adds seniority, category, remote type, skills, estimated HKD salary range with confidence, and a <=3-sentence description_summary. Jobs with no description get an empty summary string, never a hallucinated one.

nodes.label: Salary Clamping Against Anchor Tables
nodes.rationale: clamp_salary() in salary_clamp.py is the #4 most-connected function in the codebase (47 edges). Every AI estimate is checked against real Hays/Adecco/PersolKelly anchor tables in salary_guidlines/ so DeepSeek cannot hallucinate a HK$2M graduate salary. salary_audit.py re-checks past estimates for drift.

nodes.label: Finance-Only Tech Filter

nodes.label: Recruiter Posts (Secret Market) Subsystem

nodes.label: Seven-Week HK Finance Posting Panel
nodes.rationale: 13,504 postings observed across 196 employers, 8 sources and 33 scrape dates, 2026-06-01 to 2026-07-25; 4,986 active rows, ~3,611 distinct roles. Computed against a consistent jobs.db snapshot taken 2026-07-25 20:01 HKT while the pipeline was mid-run, plus the 10 archived snapshots in data/backups/.

nodes.label: Evidential Status Grading
nodes.rationale: Every claim carries a grade — Well supported, Directional, Not supported, Artefact, Not usable — and nothing is asserted above its grade. The cross-section (what roles exist, what they pay, what they ask) is solid; the time series is not, and publishing a 'who's hiring' leaderboard today would report scraper behaviour as market behaviour.

nodes.label: Zero-Observation Defect
nodes.rationale: 323 of 1,314 company-days in the stable window record exactly zero jobs — adapter failures, not empty careers pages. AXA reads 44, 48, 0, 53, 0, 52…; Zurich reads 18, 20, 0, 20, 0, 20. A zero followed by full recovery is a failed fetch recorded as a fact.

nodes.label: Pagination Fingerprint Defect
nodes.rationale: Counts cluster on exactly 10 and exactly 20 far beyond chance (56 and 29 observations, 22 companies landing there repeatedly). Those are page sizes, not job counts — Goldman Sachs reads 59, 49, 10, 10, 18, 10…; Standard Chartered 45, 67, 10, 20, 72…. A paginated fetch stopping after page one is recorded as a collapse in hiring.

nodes.label: jobs_added Re-Seed Defect
nodes.rationale: In 9.7% of observations jobs_added equals the full job count instead of the day-over-day increase, re-declaring every open role as new. HKEX moved 119 to 124 roles on 23 July but logged jobs_added = 124, producing a phantom 'HKEX added 244 roles' when summed.

nodes.label: Retracted Hiring-Velocity Analysis
nodes.rationale: Hiring-velocity and net-mover analyses were computed, inspected and discarded. Only 55.9% of the 1,314 company-days survive as clean; 24.6% of observations are zero and 32.9% of firms swing >=50% daily. Until the zero-guard and pagination fixes land, any company-level trend read from job_history is measuring the scraper.

nodes.label: Stable-Roster Window (16–25 July)
nodes.rationale: The panel opens on 1 June tracking 28 companies and closes tracking 146, so total counts rise for reasons unrelated to the market. Every time-based figure is confined to the nine scrape dates where the roster is constant at 146.

nodes.label: Observation-Window Trap
nodes.rationale: A first pass reported 28-day median life for ATS feeds against 2 days for eFinancialCareers. Invalid: Workday and Eightfold have 55 days of observation, eFC only 11, so only short-lived eFC postings can appear closed. The giveaway was 86 active eFC listings over 30 days old. The correction — shown rather than hidden — is a fixed 7-day follow-up horizon applied identically to every source.

nodes.label: Uniform 7-Day Closure Rate
nodes.rationale: Measured identically: Eightfold 0.4% (n=237), Workday 5.6% (n=125), JobsDB 24.4% (n=4,653), LinkedIn 39.8% (n=211), eFinancialCareers 76.9% (n=65). At 14 days Eightfold is still 7.3% and Workday 6.7%. eFC's level is indicative, its rank solid.

nodes.label: Listing Churn Measures Board Hygiene, Not Fills
nodes.rationale: Each source's disappearance rate is mostly a property of its own retention policy. Only employer-ATS feeds track the actual role, and they say finance roles stay open for weeks — under 6% close within a week. A vanished aggregator listing is weak evidence that a role is gone.
nodes.norm_label: listing churn measures board hygiene, not fills

nodes.label: JobsDB 30-Day Delisting Timer
nodes.rationale: In a like-for-like survival curve (both scraped since 31 May) the JobsDB curve does not decay — it falls vertically to exactly zero at day 30. That is a retention policy rendered as a survival curve. The ATS curve declines gradually and continues past day 30, which is what a real hiring process looks like. Indeed by contrast leaves dead listings up for years.

nodes.label: Re-Listing Under a New ID
nodes.rationale: For 81 of 277 eFC listings closed since 1 July (29.2%) the same employer still has an identical title live under a different listing ID — HKEX and DBS cycling Treasures Relationship Manager and Post-Trade Systems roles. Because the test requires exact title match and only counts roles live today, 29.2% is a floor, not an estimate. Users currently see these as expired.

nodes.label: 60-Day Stale Tail on the Live Board
nodes.rationale: Of 4,852 active postings with a usable date, only 13.6% were posted in the last three days while 15.6% are over two months old. Since ATS evidence shows most roles resolving well inside two months, much of that tail is filled roles nobody retracted — a default freshness filter would improve perceived quality more than any new source.
nodes.norm_label: 60-day stale tail on the live board

nodes.label: 3.5x Weekday Posting Rhythm
nodes.rationale: 1,785 postings per weekday against 509 per weekend day (8,923 vs 1,018 total), holding across every source independently including employer-ATS feeds where the employer's own system writes the timestamp. Eightfold recorded zero weekend postings in the entire window.

nodes.label: Thursday Peak is an Instrument Artefact
nodes.rationale: Chi-square against uniform weekdays gives 21.51 on 4 df, past the 9.49 critical value — but with 9,941 observations almost any wobble would be significant. The real test is replication across independent sources, and it fails: the entire effect lives in JobsDB (23.5%), while LinkedIn 16.9%, Workday 17.2% and Eightfold 18.1% sit below uniform. An effect that reverses sign when you change measuring instrument is a property of the instrument.
nodes.norm_label: thursday peak is an instrument artefact

nodes.label: 'Apply Within the Hour' Null Result
nodes.rationale: Tested on 665 live postings carrying LinkedIn applicant counts: Spearman rho = 0.029, t = 0.76, nowhere near 1.96. Week-one postings average 37.5 applicants, month-two 46.2, and weeks 3–4 are the crowded bucket — a shape indistinguishable from noise. It does not mean applying early is harmful; it means there is no evidence a same-day application beats a considered one three days later.

nodes.label: Survivorship Caveat on Applicant Counts
nodes.rationale: Applicant counts are only observed on postings still open. If heavily-applied roles close faster, the crowded ones drop out of view and the true age-competition slope is partly hidden. The honest conclusion is that the panel cannot support the urgency claim, not that urgency is disproven.

nodes.label: 28% Row-Count vs Opportunity-Count Gap
nodes.rationale: Of 4,986 active rows, 2,304 are flagged cross-posted and 1,375 of those are suppressed as non-primary duplicates, so the board represents roughly 3,611 distinct roles — the visible board is ~28% smaller than its row count.

nodes.label: Unaudited Fuzzy Cross-Post Matcher
nodes.rationale: Exact dedup_hash matching finds only 146 jobs on two sources; the other ~2,150 of 2,304 merge decisions come entirely from the fuzzy title matcher, which has never been precision-audited against a labelled sample. If it over-merges, real distinct roles are hidden from users. Recommendation: hand-label 200 pairs and measure.

nodes.label: Sole-Source Coverage Per Adapter
nodes.rationale: Every source is the sole home of a meaningful block of roles — dropping JobsDB would cost 1,715 roles nothing else covers, dropping the paid LinkedIn-posts feed 196. No single source makes the others redundant, which is the strongest available justification for the multi-adapter architecture.

nodes.label: Seniority Salary Ladder
nodes.rationale: Model estimates, not advertised salaries: of 9,057 estimates only 62 (0.7%) are high confidence, 8,282 medium, 713 low. Calibrated against Hays 2026 anchors and clamped by a deterministic rule, so the shape is dependable and the levels only indicative. Rungs separate cleanly with no overlap — the best evidence the enrichment behaves sensibly — and the steepest jump is mid to senior, where the floor rises 64% from HK$34.9k to HK$57.3k.

nodes.label: Mandate Skills Command the Premium
nodes.rationale: Against a HK$43,000 market median: investment advisory +74% (75 postings), team leadership +49%, portfolio management +40%, stakeholder management +23%, risk management +22% — while the highest-frequency skills, regulatory compliance (1,043 postings, 21.5%) and relationship management (810), sit at the median. Ubiquity and premium are close to opposites: what everyone must have prices like a floor, not a differentiator.

nodes.label: Skill Casing Fragmentation
nodes.rationale: The enricher does not normalise casing, so 'Stakeholder Management', 'Stakeholder management' and 'stakeholder management' are stored as three separate skills. 2,549 labels collapse into far fewer canonical terms once folded; every figure in the report is post-normalisation, the raw database table is not, and the product's own filters therefore understate every skill frequency.

nodes.label: Secret Market Unit Economics
nodes.rationale: 578 posts ingested, 196 promoted to live roles, 100% of which appear on no other source, for US$4.21 of the US$30 cap — 14% of budget for ~4% of the active board, about 2 US cents per exclusive role. The best-performing source in the system. The constraint on scaling is watchlist coverage, not budget: the last run polled 59 recruiters and 8 failed.
